summary: Iteration 336 - QC Live Board enhancements (Reject Alerts, Shift Report PDF, Batch Drilldown, Trend Sparklines) verified end-to-end on backend + frontend. 9/9 new backend pytest cases pass; existing 9 QC Station regression tests still pass. UI verified: shift report PDF downloads, defect trends sparkline renders, alert_emails settings input persists, drill modal opens with stage-by-stage history (QC1: 18 crates / 19 rejected) and reason chips + timestamps, wall mode toggles dark theme, over-threshold red card badge shown at 12.5%. Alert flow: reject_alert_sent=true set atomically on threshold cross (25% > 5%), remains immutable on subsequent taps (verified via /qc-sessions/active). No 500s or new errors in backend logs during the flow.
critical_code_review_comments: Alert idempotency uses a single atomic $set with reject_alert_sent guard — correct and race-safe. Good pattern.

qc-shift-report and qc-reason-trends use ISO string prefix bounds ($gte day, $lt day+'T24') to slice inspections — works because inspected_at is stored as ISO string with 'T' separator. If inspected_at ever changes to datetime type, these queries silently return empty. Consider a small comment or a datetime-aware alt query.

Sparkline component (SVG polyline) doesn't set a fixed viewBox height for very-tall single-hour spikes; visually still fine since it fills the SVG height, but a note-worthy edge case if only one hour has data (which happens today).
DrillModal fetches history on open — no loading skeleton visible (just re-renders when data arrives). Minor UX; not a blocker.
qc-shift-report PDF uses reportlab; date validation missing — an invalid date param would still generate a PDF for that garbage day. Not a security issue but could be tightened.
